subject: Discovery recap — reserved capacity: throughput, isolation, and burst criteria
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@datascale.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 19 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap — reserved capacity: throughput, isolation, and burst criteria

Hi Alyssa — thanks for taking time earlier. Short recap from our call and the concrete asks we captured. Please confirm anything I missed.

Pain points you described:
- Unpredictable token costs and 95th pct latency spikes during batch replays (weekly batch window).
- Regulatory requirement for workload isolation: model inference must run in tenant-dedicated pools with separate logging and keying.
- Existing infra (in-house endpoint fabric) struggles to scale from 200 TPS steady to 1,200 TPS burst for short (~5–10 min) windows.

Current stack and constraints:
- Inference currently on self-managed servers behind a homegrown queue; models are 35–70B parameter family (quantized to int8 in prod).
- KV cache is partially implemented; prefix caching not enabled in traffic spikes.
- Encryption keys managed in-house (HSM) — DataScale needs a path that preserves key control.

Success criteria for a Dedicated pilot (what will make this a win):
1) Stable 95th percentile generation latency <= 450ms for 512-token avg requests at 200 TPS steady.
2) Support predictable burst to 1,200 TPS for up to 10 minutes with documented failure/fallback behavior.
3) Tenant isolation with separated audit logs and KMS integration (customer-managed key).
4) Cost profile target: <= 35% reduction in $/query vs their current infra baseline (after batching/kv tuning).

Next steps (owner / ETA):
- Priyom: send this recap + annotated requirements spreadsheet (attached) and a preliminary pilot SOW draft — EOD Monday (2026-07-20).
- Alyssa: confirm the steady vs peak TPS windows (can you break down typical daily cadence?) and share any SOC2 evidence/contacts we should use — by Tue 2026-07-21.
- Ben/Grace: can you review the attachment and flag any engine/quantization constraints before I draft the SOW? (Ben: perf knobs; Grace: security integration).

Attachments: DataScale_Pilot_Requirements.xlsx (rows: expected qps, payload sizes, seq lengths, preferred quantization), proposal-draft-v1.pdf (skeleton SOW).

— Priyom
Priyom Das

Alyssa C: "Our spikes are short but brutal — we see latency and cost go through the roof when replays hit the same models. Isolation is non-negotiable."

From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@datascale.io>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 09:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — reserved capacity: throughput, isolation, and burst criteria

Thanks, Priyom — summary looks right. A couple of clarifications: 

- Steady state: 180–220 TPS (mostly short requests, avg 120 tokens).
- Burst pattern: typically 08:45–09:00 and 17:30–17:40 PST for batch replays and customer report generation — bursts to 1,100–1,300 TPS lasting 6–12 minutes.
- Models: two families in scope for pilot (Triton-compat 40B and 70B int8 variants).
- KMS: we use HashiCorp Vault backed by an HSM. We need a flow where keys never leave our control; Redwood's private deployment is preferable but we want to understand a hybrid (dedicated pool + customer KMS).

I'll attach the internal traffic histogram and a small excerpt of our SOC2 checklist (redacted). Expect to send by EOD.

Also, can you include a quick note on failure modes we should expect if bursts exceed capacity (queueing, async fallback to smaller model, or token-dropping)? That will help our infra team sign off.

— Alyssa
Alyssa Chen
Head of Platform Engineering, DataScale
alyssa@datascale.io | +44 20 7946 0812

Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Discovery recap — reserved capacity: throughput, isolation, and burst criteria (DataScale) — action items

Ben/Grace/Sean — forwarding the recap + Alyssa's confirm. Key asks for our pilot SOW: predictable burst up to 1.3k TPS, HSM-backed KMS integration, and clearly documented fallbacks.

Summary of technical asks for your review:
- Throughput/SLOs: 200 TPS steady with 95th <=450ms for 512 tokens; burst to 1,300 TPS for ~10 min with defined ramp/backoff behavior.
- Isolation: tenant-dedicated GPU pools, separate logging pipelines, per-tenant KMS handshake.
- Fallback policy preferences from customer: priority is to avoid rejecting customer-facing traffic — prefer async queue with model-downscale fallback (smaller quantized model) before token-dropping.

Action items: 
- Ben: confirm if our runtime can guarantee the 95th pctl at 200 TPS with their model flavors (35–70B int8) and outline needed perf knobs (batching params, KV cache warmup).
- Grace: confirm what we need to support HashiCorp Vault/HSM integration in a Dedicated deployment and what minimal evidence we require for SOC2.
- Sean: draft a short appendix for the SOW describing burst policy options (canary fallback, model substitution, region-level redirect).

I've attached the spreadsheet Alyssa mentioned and the initial SOW skeleton (proposal-draft-v1.pdf). Please review and leave comments in the Drive link; I plan to send the first SOW draft to DataScale by EOD today if feasible.

Thanks — Priyom

Attachments: DataScale_Pilot_Requirements.xlsx, proposal-draft-v1.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Discovery recap — reserved capacity: throughput, isolation, and burst criteria (DataScale) — action items

All — quick read. Two high-level notes before I dig in: 
1) Engine should hit 95th <=450ms at 200 TPS for int8 40B with aggressive batching and warmed KV cache; 70B may need slight relax or more GPUs pinned per pool. I'll validate exact GPU counts with infra.
2) For bursts, we should propose a multi-tiered policy: (a) short-term autoscale to reserved burst capacity, (b) model substitution to smaller quantized variant, (c) region fallback to secondary pool, (d) as last resort, queue with SLA-aware draining.

I'll add specifics to the sheet by noon and flag any infra blockers.

— Ben
